names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 8 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Διονύσιος ο Ιερομάρτυρας», with the rank words left off.

death.note: saint.gr: «Ο Άγιος Ιερομάρτυρας Διονύσιος ήταν Επίσκοπος και μαρτύρησε στη Βιέννη μετά το 193 μ.Χ.» The page's own «μετά το 193» is a lower bound and nothing more, and the head line gives «(; - 193)»; the open upper bound is the finding, not a gap.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 8ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Διονύσιος ο Ιερομάρτυρας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 8 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **The slug and the display name carry the day and not the city on purpose**: the page says he was a bishop and that he was martyred at Vienne — «ήταν Επίσκοπος και μαρτύρησε στη Βιέννη» — and it does *not* say he was bishop *of* Vienne, so no `office` is stored and «of Vienne» is kept out of the name. The name sweep raised more than a dozen Dionysii and **not one of them is this man**: none of the corpus's Dionysii is a bishop martyred at Vienne, and none is kept on 8 Μαΐου. No relics, no judge, no manner of death, no hymn. **`locations` are left out**, because a city of martyrdom is not a city the page places him in otherwise, and the date has an open upper bound.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
